goal: Release execution capacity from real process exit without pretending work completed
invariants: A bound execution host ends after one result while planning chats stay persistent
The native host records actual exit independently of its daemon connection
Canonical run/session validation and first-terminal-state preservation fence exit commits
Failed commits retain receipts and refuse accidental restart of completed work
Claim capacity becomes reusable while the unfinished bead remains open
Saved checkpoint answers and exits resume through the normal capacity reservation
An unrelated bad receipt cannot stop other exit reconciliation
Socket loss preserves live custody and permits adoption of the same process
Native checkpoints do not borrow another run's Codex thread
Actual fake Codex hosts end their runs and fresh replacements start independent threads
A durable physical-exit receipt carries the unaccepted terminal report to the current planning Commander
Missing final reports become explicit review obligations, not silent work completion or human decisions
Blocking question checkpoints preserve their exact resume source instead of becoming deliverable results
The actual detached PostgreSQL cockpit renders the canonical Commander review wait with no legacy Manager window
Terminal columns consume the canonical snapshot for execution counts, spinners and scope status; a database error clears the healthy saved frame
